title: the T.35 payload buffer was allocated to its exact size, so a padded reader ran past it
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a reader that may read up to AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE past the payload runs off an exactly sized allocation
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_buffer_alloc, no inner layer.
fidelity: model consumer, real constant. AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE is FFmpeg's own 64, and the case asserts that the unpadded allocation ends before the padded read does.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/cbs_av1_syntax_template.c carries av_buffer_alloc(current->payload_size + AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE) together with the memset of that padding. The pre-fix line, av_buffer_alloc(current->payload_size), is at 8553e6ef57^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

spatial.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-capstone/: **CAUGHT** at ffh_read_probe_u8+0x38 -- cause 5, a bounds violation on a load; pc=0xc020eaf4, address=0xc025211b. CheriBSD did NOT catch this crossing: its malloc bounds to a size class and the crossing landed in the slack. level0 bounds to the request, so there is none.  Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. Arm: the level0 heap: malloc narrows the returned capability to exactly the bytes requested (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS), and free only marks the block free. controls in the same boot: one-past-the-end write CAUGHT (cause=7 pc=0xc020e5b8 address=0xc0251768), use-after-free read RETURNED, clean access RETURNED. Image 0ed8b2d83936d740. Predicted before the run (pre-registration 60f1c5be25a5); the prediction held.
spatial.prediction: PREDICTED, not measured: added after this corpus's last platform run. The crossing leaves a direct allocation, so a per-allocation bound SHOULD fault. On CheriBSD that is conditional on the usable size for this request -- a size class is a step function and the capability length must be read in-guest before the arm is called either way.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **NOT CAUGHT, and clean here is NOT a negative result about the defect.** The sequence COMPLETES, exit status 0, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_read_probe_u8 0x1021c6` from the ELF -- so the probe was found and simply never faulted. THE MECHANISM: malloc bounds a capability to the allocator's USABLE size and not to the request, so a crossing shorter than the gap to the next size class stays inside the same allocation and no capability check can see it. This is a property of the allocator's granularity, not of the bug. tools/size-class-audit.py reports this case ABSORBED from the measured request size, and the two agree. The Capstone arms are the discriminating ones here.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from av_buffer_alloc with no inner allocator between it and the platform, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the other rows here cross by a mis-shaped index; this one crosses because the allocation omits padding that FFmpeg's own readers are documented to require, so the index is correct and the SIZE is wrong.
